JOOLA Infinity Balance - Advanced Performance Ping Pong Paddle - Competition Ready - Table Tennis Racket for High-Level Training - Designed to Optimize Spin and Control I ordered the following for review:
JOOLA Infinity Balance - Advanced Performance Ping Pong Paddle - Competition Ready - Table Tennis Racket for High-Level Training - Designed to Optimize Spin and Control (Method 38)

JOOLA Infinity Edge - Tournament Performance Ping Pong Paddle w/Pro Carbon Technology - Black Rubber on Both Sides - Competition Ready - Table Tennis Racket for Advanced Training - Designed for Speed (Driver 42 Blue Handle)

JOOLA Omega Speed - Table Tennis Racket for Advanced Training with Flared Handle - Tournament Level Ping Pong Paddle with Torrent 33 Table Tennis Rubber- Designed for Speed

JOOLA Infinity Edge - Tournament Performance Ping Pong Paddle w/Pro Carbon Technology - Black Rubber on Both Sides - Competition Ready - Table Tennis Racket for Advanced Training - Designed for Speed (Driver 42 Red Handle)

JOOLA Omega Strata - Table Tennis Racket with Flared Handle - Tournament Level Ping Pong Paddle with Riff 34 Table Tennis Rubber - Designed for Spin .

It’s been years since I played Ping Pong and back then I never had the opportunity to use, and was not even familiar with the Joola brand unfortunately. As I have had time to use and play with these 5 different Joola Ping Pong paddles, I must say that they are all incredible compared to any other Ping Pong paddle I have ever used. The quality and performance far exceeds my previous experiences.

Each of these paddles have been designed for a specific purpose which include speed, spin and control. Now not being a professional, I can not “honestly” say that I notice the difference between any of these five different paddles, in any of the different design aspects while using them. However, I can honestly say that visually I can tell the difference by the different rubber padding (sandwiched between the inner and outer rubber) used in each. Some have a slightly different thickness, weight, color and I assume different “springiness”. With that said, each and every one of them have performed absolutely stellar in every way for my, and my family’s play style. Personally they all have incredible spin, speed and control capabilities. They are all built with beautiful build quality, and designed with comfort and balance in mind. I especially love the resin looking inlaid logo at the end of the handles. I realise that it doesn’t make a performance difference but it just ads to the overall beauty and gives each paddle a quality looking finish.

Overall I feel quite privileged to have had the opportunity to use and experience the Joola brand and share my opinions, though I feel absolutely unqualified to have done so. Just know that if you have never used or played with a “quality” Ping Pong paddle, you are truly missing out, and this Joola brand will be the only brand I choose from here on out! The quality is impeccable!!
text_fidelity_b: JOOLA Infinity Balance - Advanced Performance Ping Pong Paddle - Competition Ready - Table Tennis Racket for High-Level Training - Designed to Optimize Spin and Control

text_fidelity_a:
Genuine Fred Howligans Dog Bandana, Large, Red I was excited to order these bandanas for my adult Corgi, Skip, and my new puppy I'm picking up soon! I got the red and the navy blue and even though there is no option to choose the size you want, based on other reviews, I was expecting the red to arrive in size small and this navy blue to be size medium/large. That is not the case. The blue one arrived first, in size small and unfortunately is too small for Skip. I can get the collar on him, but the ends barely overlap, leaving just enough space for the velcro to catch and the front triangle of material is laughably small on him.

I love the adorable print! There's images of squirrels, fire hydrants, balls, steaks and paw prints and cute sayings.. "Quite Fetching", "Ain't Too Proud To Beg". "Smell Ya later", You Gonna Eat That?", I'm All Ears!", "Gotta Run!", "Yo Dawg!" and "Shake On It". The product description claims that "the pattern is printed in reflective ink". I did not find this to be the case. The ink is silver and while it is shiny and kind of metallic, reflective it is not. This is not a deterrent for me, but may be for others.

I do like the velcro closure! I usually steer clear of dog bandanas because I don't like having to tie them on which makes the dog look silly with the two ends sticking out.. and I have rarely had luck finding a bandana that's the right size to my dog. I usually end up with a too large bandana (Corgi's a small-ish) that I fold in half into the standard triangle, tie it around his neck and then, not only does he have those "wings" sticking out from the tie, but he also is dwarfed by the size of the triangle in the front. My dogs don't need a bib or a necktie. LOL!

The sizing on this navy blue bandana (I have yet to receive the red one and am now quite curious to see what size shows up) is perfect for a smaller dog. I planned on Skip wearing this navy blue one, but it seems it will be given to my new Corgi puppy. The size small that I received will fit him properly and look right. I can only hope that I receive the red in a size medium/large so Skip gets to wear one too. If not, then the new pup will be off to a great start in the wardrobe department!

Bottom line... These are quite cute, very well made, the velcro is strong enough to hold through a round of scratching and seems as though it would hold during light play (we'll put that to the real test when our new puppy arrives!) and the size of the bandana itself (referring to the navy blue only) seems correct. But not being able to select the size you will receive is just shocking. It almost feels like a shot in the dark to order this - what size will I receive this time? That is not how anyone likes to shop and I'm surprised there is no size selection available for this reason.
text_fidelity_b: Genuine Fred Howligans Dog Bandana, Large, Red

Franklin Sports Arctic Trails Hiking Poles - Lightweight - Anti Shock Technology - Great for All Skill Levels I've had a set of MSR trek poles for over a decade now. I've used them to travel though the Zion river, down and up the grand canyon, through forests of sequoias and so on. They've always worked well, but there's been newer tech since I first bought them.

So I put them side by side for a comparison. Here's how's the two stack up.
They both operate in the same way as far as extending and turning to lock them.
They are both clearly marked so you always knows your set length.
As shown in the photo, the MSRs are a bit taller when extended. They're both just about the same height when collapsed.
The MSRs did not come with option for swappable end caps.
The hand grips on these are softer.
As shown in the other photo, the tip shield on the MSRs are indexed so they interlock. That keeps them from swinging around.
And probably the biggest difference is that these have shock absorption. There's just enough spring to take off some of the abruptness of planting these down on unstable footing without there being too much travel to throw off stability.

So overall, they work well. They're an improvement overt the old ones in some ways. In others, they're not.
text_fidelity_b: Franklin Sports Arctic Trails Hiking Poles - Lightweight - Anti Shock Technology - Great for All Skill Levels

Backyard Champs Corn Hole Outdoor Game USA Stars and Stripes: 2 Regulation MDF Cornhole Boards and 8 Bean Bags, 2 x 3 Foot One game that seems to be quite popular nowadays is cornhole. It’s a simple game and I often find it at local taverns, breweries, etc that have a large outdoor space. It’s also the type of game I find at friend’s houses and so it made sense to get a set of my own, the Backyard Champs Wood Cornhole Set.

With the American flag design on the two cornhole boards, this set has a patriotic look, which adds to its appeal, since it is certainly better than the plain cornhole boards so common in backyards across America. The boards come complete with bean bags, too, but there is no net to catch the bags, like with some cornhole sets. With this set, the bags will go through the opening and hit the surface beneath, so you need to make sure to place the boards on a reasonably clean surface.

The wood construction of this cornhole set is nice and I like how they attach together with Velcro. There are Velcro strips on the backs of the boards and this makes it easier to carry the boards around. The Velcro keeps them together, so when it comes time to pack up and leave, you almost feel like you’re carrying a single item. They don’t weigh too much either, so it takes little effort to move the boards from place to place.

Backyard Champs Wood Cornhole Set is easy to set up and play straight from the box. The sturdy boards are made to last and the 8 included bean bags weigh 12 oz each, which is heavy enough to make them good for this type of game; less likely to slide past the opening and slide off of the board. The legs fold flat against the backside, so attaching the boards together with the Velcro is easy.

Cornhole is a popular backyard game and since I play it frequently when I go places, I decided it was time to get a game of my own. Backyard Champs Wood Cornhole Set is a very good cornhole game set with a nice design and good durability. It’s a game I recommend for anyone who likes simple, outdoor entertainment for kids and guests.
text_fidelity_b: Backyard Champs Corn Hole Outdoor Game USA Stars and Stripes: 2 Regulation MDF Cornhole Boards and 8 Bean Bags, 2 x 3 Foot

MIER Lanshan Ultralight Tent 3-Season Backpacking Tent for 1-Person or 2-Person Camping, Trekking, Kayaking, Climbing, Hiking UPADATED AGAIN: I have purchased both the 1 and 2 person tent. Seems like very well quality and lightweight. However, the ONE thing that is bad about BOTH tents is the way the end tie outs are sewn and sealed. The tents BOTH leak at the tie out points. This is due to the way they are sealed. It seams as if the seam seal was applied FIRST and then the tie outs sewn into the fabric. This allows water to come through the stitching and leak into the tent. POOR DESIGN. I have remedied this by using seam sealant on ALL stitch points for the tie outs. So, word of caution for everyone owning and buying these tents. MAKE SURE YOU SEAM SEAL EVERY TIE OUT POINT. Once you do that, this tent should be waterproof.

UPDATE: I set this tent up in my yard to test it for waterproof and durability. We had a rain event that came through. No heavy storms. Just light to medium rain that only lasted 10 or 15 minutes. The tent leaked at both ends where the tie outs are sewn into the fabric. These points are seam sealed, so I do not know why or how it leaked at both points. The water on the floor of the tent was about the size of a quarter.
I have since sprayed all of the fly seams and the tie out points with silicone treatment. When we get another rain storm coming through, I will set it up again for another test to see if the spray will keep the tie out points from leaking.
Also, both sides and the rear of the fly, down at the edge, collect water and allow it to pool up. This is a design flaw. I had the tent as tight as I could get it, without damaging the material. The water pooled up around the bottom edge looked like a small moat, and could lead to large amounts of water to run under the tent. This could soak through the floor and get your sleeping gear wet.
I fixed this issue with some micro tarp clamps and 550 cord. I attached one at each end, and two in the rear, one on each side between the rear stake out point and each corner. So 4 total. When I set the tent up again for another rain test, I will update with pictures.
So far, this tent was NOT the tent that all the hype was about. The ONLY positive thing so far, is that it is a true double wall tent, and that will keep condensation out of the sleeping area.

I have not used this tent yet, only set it up. However, with just having set it up, I can see that I will probably like this tent. But, one thing I would like to have seen with it, is more fabric at the vestibule. When set up by the directions, the edge of the vestibule is quite high off of the ground. This would allow for good ventilation during a summer night, but in a rain storm, I would be afraid of rain being blown in.
I have it set up in the yard, and we have a chance of rain today/tonight, so once I let it get rained on and take it out on a trip, I will update my review.
text_fidelity_b: MIER Lanshan Ultralight Tent 3-Season Backpacking Tent for 1-Person or 2-Person Camping, Trekking, Kayaking, Climbing, Hiking

text_fidelity_a:
ACCUSPLIT AX740 PRO MEMORY (50) DUAL LINE STOPWATCH I often have three or 4 different workout groups going on at the same time and I have two of the older model 740MX watches and two of the newest AX740's to help me manage it all. What I like best about this watch is that after hitting the split button which I do at the beginning of every repeat in a set, I can hit the release button and the watch will show BOTH the Total Running Time AND the running repeat time. So if I am running a set of 100's on 1:20 I hit the split button at every 1:20, then hit the release button, it shows me the running repeat time so that I can eyeball the splits during the repeat and I can shout out times as they are coming in. It also shows the number of repeats so that I never lose count of the number of repeats. So with multiple groups and multiple watches it really helps me stay organized and allows me to give better feedback to the swimmers. I have had the two 740MX's for 10 years now and have used them nearly every day and often twice a day. Recently one or the other will blank out occassionally so I have purchased the newer AX740. I am not mentioning the blanking out as a problem but more of a testament that they have lasted this long under heavy use.

These are also wonderful watches for swim meets especially when you have the luxury of one watch per swimmer. Hit the split, write it down (or let the memory save it for later), hit release and see the total running time as well as the split running time.

If there is one drawback to this watch, it's that reset is made by holding down the start button for 2 seconds -- which seems like forever when you are trying to run a bunch of individuals doing one at a time 25's and you want to get ready for the next swimmer NOW. The older versions had a similar reset but it was about 1.3 seconds, the newer AX740 is a full 2 seconds. Sometimes I think my older watches are beginning to fail because I hold down the split button as hard as I can wishfulling thinking that it will speed up the reset. A light touch does the same and may lead to a longer life of the watch.
text_fidelity_b: ACCUSPLIT AX740 PRO MEMORY (50) DUAL LINE STOPWATCH

Dynaplug Racer Pro Bicycle Tire Repair Tool 100% USA Made (Orange) I did the Unbound Gravel 200 and, like many others during the race, got a flat tire. The sharp Flint Hills rock sliced about a 3/8 in cut in my sidewall around 45 miles in. I run inserts in my tubeless tire setup, so I really didn’t want to have to put a tube in because (1) it is really hard to get the tire off and (2) I didn’t want to have to carry the sealant covered insert 30 miles until the next checkpoint.

I wasn’t sure if the Dynaplug would get the tire to seal or how long it would hold due to the size of the cut. I’ve had smaller sidewall cuts that regular bacon strips couldn’t fix. After using 2 plugs and spinning the wheel on its side a few times, I was very pleased to see the tire held air - and it held for the next 155 miles to the finish.

CamelBak Podium Chill Insulated Bike Water Bottle 21 oz, Teal I am an avid cyclist and have a lot of the older camelbak podium series bottles which were great but also somewhat annoying because the valve had a tendency to get moldy quickly (especially if you use gatorade or other sugary sport drink mixes), and the valve assembly was quite difficult to disassemble for cleaning.

The new redesigned camelbak valve on these is a huge improvement over the older ones, they seem to be more resistant to getting moldy in the first place.. and if they do it is quick and easy to disassemble for cleaning! Great job camelbak!

My only qualm with these bottles is that the plastic is very soft and gets marred/scratched very easily. This was kind of the case with the older camelbak bottles also but it seems even worse on these newer ones. It doesn't affect the function of the bottles so its not a huge issue but just kind of annoying that these look old and beat up after one or two rides whereas I have some other (non-camelbak) bottles that are several years old and still look practically new. That said, those other bottles use harder plastic which is more rigid and more difficult to squeeze, making them harder to drink from, and the ease of squeezing out a large amount of liquid is what makes the camelbak bottles so great, so its a tradeoff I'm willing to make..

I've noticed some reviewers complaining about them not fitting well in bottle cages but I've never had issues on any of my bikes, I use arundel cages on most of them but I have also have some specialized and lezyne cages.
text_fidelity_b: CamelBak Podium Chill Insulated Bike Water Bottle 21 oz, Teal

Mountain House Classic Chili Mac with Beef | Freeze Dried Backpacking & Camping Food | 3 Servings I have tried a number of mountain house meals, and absolutely adore the fact that they have a 30 year shelf life, really sturdy solid packaging, and that they are so easy to prepare. They are also incredibly delicious! When rehydrated, the quality level tastes like something you would get from a roadside diner, which is to say, really very tasty in kind of a lowbrow way.

I shared this chili mac and beef entrée with my children. We had it with some vegetables from the garden on the side to freshen it up, because there aren't really any vegetables in here. There were ample enough portions of meat and pasta, and enough sauce and flavoring to go around. I was really impressed with how well they managed to bring all of the flavors together, and how well everything rehydrated.

I will advise that you should definitely use the hottest boiling water possible to make this, because I found that when my water is merely simmering when I pour it in, sometimes the center of the meat chunks or bigger pieces do not rehydrate as well as I would hope. However, when done as directed, these really are great.

The portion size was generous enough to feed a 40-year-old woman (myself) and two small children, with a pile of vegetables on the side. If you are not having vegetables on the side, I would not try to share.

1) Opening. I note that a lot of people had issues opening, and it's true that if you have any hand issues (i.e. arthritis) it may be tough. But outside of that, I have to say I just used a regular screwdriver and opened it in about 15-20 seconds just by sticking it under the lip, prying a little, moving it to the side and repeating. I was pleasantly surprised at how easy and quick and painless it was after reading some of the comments. I suppose it's possible some lids are tougher than others, so perhaps your mileage will vary on this, but certainly not an issue for us.

2) Packaging of veggies. They come in pretty good size quantities, but bags are resealable (and nicely so--easy to open and reseal but it's a tight seal so no concerns) so you can use what you want and save the rest. We'll take some camping with us and just use another resealable bag

3) Taste: Quite good. No strange or odd taste, no aftertaste, no mushiness or blandness. In fact, I'd absolutely say you could eat these as snacks out of the bag. We did that with the broccoli.

Whether you use it for camping, for a quick toss into soup, or store for emergencies (not a bad idea), this is a good product. Strong 4.

BikingMyWay Classic Bike Safety Light Set (2PCS) - Front Safety Light Black Shell White Light - Rear Safety Light Black Shell Red Light - High Power High Brightness LED - 240 Degree Visibility - Three Working Modes: Fast Flash, Slow Flash, Steady - Aluminum Shell, Durable and Flexible Silicone Band - Water Resistant - Can be Mounted on Handlebar, Seat Riser, Fork, Backpack, Helmet and More This is a very nice set of bike safety lights. They are super simple to install - if you can stretch a rubber band you have all the skills needed to install this. The mounting band is made of (I assume) silicone, so it stretches easily and holds tight when fastened. I overstretched the band to see if it would break and it did not - very sturdy material. No tools are needed for installation, and it can be removed just as easily as it is installed.

The lights (one is red for the rear of the bike; the other is clear for the front) can be set to blink fast, blink slow, or be steady on. You cycle through the modes by pressing the light lens. Very simple to do even if you're on the bike or have gloves on.

The light is really bright. The manufacturer claims it can be seen for 200 meters, and while I didn't test that with a tape measure, I had no problems seeing the light at a considerable distance, especially when it is flashing.

The lens housing holds the 2 batteries (which are included). There's an o-ring to seal off the battery compartment from water and dirt.

The only negative is that the battery holder can be a bit finicky. There's a retention band that holds the battery in place, and it's made of very thin metal. You have to take care when putting in the batteries that the band is not bent or deformed.

The claimed battery life is 50 hours for continuous use and 150 hours for flashing use. This uses the same batteries (CR 2032) as my Kindle light, which is nice since I get those batteries in bulk at a warehouse club. Each light uses 2 batteries.

Other than the battery compartment issues, zero complaints. It's a well-designed safety light set that works well, installs easily and has good build quality for the price.

text_fidelity_a:
AMNQUERXUS Machine Washable Reflective Running Vest with LED Lights USB Rechargeable Safety Gear with Adjustable Waist, High Visibility Light Up Flashing Vest Gifts for Men Women Kids Dog Walking Sometimes where we live, it can get really scary when people drive by quickly and you are trying to go for a walk in the country to just relax. Having this vest handy is really a great item to put on both during the night time or dusk hours, or during hunting season to keep from being shot.

WHAT IS THIS LIKE?
CLOSURES
This comes with an XL vest that fits around the sides and closes. with strong velcro type closures.

FABRIC
This is a very nice mesh fabric. It allows for airflow and has a slight stretch/give to it so it is comfortable.

SIZING
This fits me and I am between a size 14 and 16 misses. If I were to put this over a winter jacket, I could still close it unless the coat is WAY too puffy.

HOW DOES THIS WORK?
POWER BOX
This is ingenious, actually. There is a little packet which recharges. It has a plug on it and also a cord that is USB to recharge it. Once it is charged, then you slip the little box unto a closed pocket which sits under a power button. The box gives a place for the power button to rest on when you press it.

LIGHTS
Once you have it connected, the button is pressed once, and you get the lights on front and back to go on. Once the lights are on, then you can make them flash fast by pressing another time. One more press makes for a slower blink, and a fourth press turns them off.

VEST
The vest itself is brilliant neon yellow. There is plenty of reflective tape all over this vest front and back. There is even a zipper pocket on the front for you to put your phone or other small items in.

BATTERY LIFE?
The battery life of this seems quite good. I have used it a few times and there is still no need for a recharge. I would say you could get a few hours of continuous use at least per charge, maybe more. My outings did not add up to that much yet.

WASHING
I am only going to handwash this without the battery pack and air dry it well before trying to use again. It will dry fast due to the fabric.

HUNTING SEASON
Around my area, fall time into winter can be dangerous. We have had our home shot by hunters by accident, and often there are inexperienced people who try to hunt and they don't pay attention to what is going on, thinking noises are deer. This vest will alert anyone in the early morning or early evening hours that there is a person there.

THE BOTTOM LINE
This is a great vest to have handy. I plan to keep using this especially through hunting season and for late night walks when i hear a car coming.

MY RATING
FIVE STARS. This is an ingenious little invention and I am glad to have it. I am considering purchasing others for the rest of the family.
text_fidelity_b: AMNQUERXUS Machine Washable Reflective Running Vest with LED Lights USB Rechargeable Safety Gear with Adjustable Waist, High Visibility Light Up Flashing Vest Gifts for Men Women Kids Dog Walking

You can screw cooking this completely if you don't know what you're doing because you'll need to know on what ratio is from the rice and water and it's always the one that will get you. I put a cup and a half of rice and washed it then put the necessary ratio then I set the Trangia burner into medium (The simmer ring set to half open) then I left it to boil for 20 minutes. 20 Minutes later, i found out that it's cooking perfectly so i took the simmer ring off then set it to really low (The simmer ring set to 1/4 of the opening) then I left it for another 7 Minutes. I was completely surprised that this cook set cooked the white rice PERFECTLY then had enough fuel left to fry me some breakfast sausages + 2 eggs sunny side up & boiled a cup of hot water for my coffee! 48 minutes total time from start to finish with everything done in between! This alone made a firm believer out of me of this cook set and now i bring it anywhere i go because it's completely different when you make your own coffee. This is now permanently sitting inside in a small cubby hole in my backpack and I cannot imagine going outside like in our public park without this. It's light enough to lug around and but just right for you to notice that it's in your backpack. The Swedes knew a good thing when they invented and made this and the Trangia Company has been making this cook sets since 1925. You don't lasts that long with a brand name like Trangia if you make questionable products made in poor craftsmanship that doesn't last. I'm telling everyone about this cook set and how convenient it is having one. Sure this cook set is not cheap but knowing that it's European made with the Best quality materials, This one clearly defines the old moniker "You Get What you paid For". A cook set that would lasts a Lifetime...GUARANTEED! A Highly recommended product and You won't be sorry having this If it cooks white rice perfectly...just imagine what else can you cook that's harder and trickier!?

text_fidelity_a: Lodge Cast Iron Melting Pot, Pre-Seasoned, 15-Ounce I actually purchased this for mixing henna for my hair rather than for barbecuing. The henna product I use instructed setting the henna in an iron pot, but I thought I could bypass this. After using henna for a couple of months, the thought occurred to me that maybe something in the interaction with the iron metal helps with the curing. Any henna user will tell you that it's an endurance test and everyone has to find their own mixer combination and timing for the results they want. I'm still experimenting, so I bought this pot per the henna instruction with the hope that it will help me get the results I wanted. I did everything in mixing the henna I had usually been doing, then applied it from my roots down about 1". Since I only have to do my roots now, the size of this pot works out. This first time that I have used the pot, the henna color result on my hair is actually a little darker, more red than before without the pot and closer to what I want. I also had kept the henna on my hair for half the time I did before because it was just too hot that day. So, there might be something, then, to the whole iron pot use. Whatever the cause for the darkening, I am continuing with this iron pot and experimenting with combinations. This size is agreeable also because it fits nicely on my small bathroom vanity as I apply the henna and it does not take up much space on my tiny kitchen counter as it cures. The long handle makes it easier to move around, because, well, small bathroom vanity and tiny kitchen counter. I would recommend this pot for anyone who does henna on their roots.
text_fidelity_b: Lodge Cast Iron Melting Pot, Pre-Seasoned, 15-Ounce

I also believe the company is using a common practice of identifying an American made product, while not outwardly saying Made in America. I understand that an American flag doesn’t always mean made here, but this style is commonly used for such purposes. Seeing as the company's profile is based out of China I would safely say this product is made there.

Swagman XTC2 Hitch Mount Bike Rack I'll try to get to the details not already mentioned multiple times:

FOLDED DIMENSIONS: 38"H x 15.5"D x 10"W when completely folded with the hitch bar removed. I was really pleased to see what a small footprint this takes up when not attached to the car. Folding takes about 40 seconds, and removing the hitch bar - if desired - takes another 60 or so and requires an allen wrench. I made a partially-sided box out of scrap wood to hold and protect this nicely behind the car in the garage when not in use.

When folded, the center bar and two side bars come to within about 1/8" of each other without touching - very nicely designed.

TIGHTENING MECHANISMS: I was delighted to see that the mechanisms to hand tighten the wheel holders are the high quality, non-abrasive clamping type, rather than the screw-down-a-machine-screw type that flakes paint and distorts metal over time.

CONSTRUCTION: All immovable joints are welded, the rubber straps on the wheel holders are very thick, and the ratcheting clamps are fantastic. The anti-wobble hitch pin works, but you'll need to carry your 19mm socket/wrench if you want to remove this at your cycling site (but it's quick and easy to fold and throw in the trunk).

LOCKING: It's been mentioned before over several reviews, but to consolidate points: One small lock will fit through the hitch pin nicely, but you need larger locks to keep the center arms from being removable. One reviewer enlarged his with a drill to make his next size larger lock fit, but I won't do the same to mine for fear of removing the finish, possibly making a weak point for rust to form. Locking the arms with the correct size lock is a great feature and a great selling point (actually, that was what finally got me to pick this one over the similar model by Hollywood Racks), but it would have been absolutely fantastic if the hitch pin and arm clamps took the same size lock so you could get a matching set that uses one key. Alternatively, I would have gladly paid a couple bucks more to have appropriate locks included.

Absolutely recommended.
text_fidelity_b: Swagman XTC2 Hitch Mount Bike Rack

text_fidelity_a:
Kryptonite KryptoFlex Looped Bike Security Cable, 7' (10mm), Grey/Orange On a 60cm bike with a very high seatpost this is long enough to lock up my saddle, rear wheel, and Vector pedal (left side only). I lock my bike with an Abus Bordo X-Plus (like a U lock but the U is in flexible segments instead of a rigid U). I put the lock around the front wheel and frame, and this short cable is enough to add a little deterrent to the bike components. I don't have any theft protection on the cockpit beyond the brake and shifter cables. As it stands, someone would have to use tools to take most things off my bike - they could get the skewers - nothing else comes to mind...

I can fit this cable in my back jeans pocket, but also I am 6'4" so IDK whether that would be true for smaller people. I wear 34" waist jeans.

I'm still searching for a way to easily/quickly carry this on the bike but so far IDK. Also fits in a jersey pocket. The velcro cable tie is a nice touch - keeps it from springing open when coiled in a pocket. I wish it was smaller. I wish there was no theft in the world.

BTW I'm sure most people know this already, but just in case this is the only text you ever read on locking up a bike: the trick to getting the most out of a double-loop cable is feeding it through one of its own loops. One end is looped around a wheel or saddle rail or whatever, and the other loop goes through the lock. That way you get double the coverage - or half the cable length - as you would putting your main lock through both loops of the cable.

HTH,
Michael
text_fidelity_b: Kryptonite KryptoFlex Looped Bike Security Cable, 7' (10mm), Grey/Orange

ACCUSPLIT Survivor II - S2XL Stopwatch, Clock I use a stopwatch a lot to time my exercise. This is the best stopwatch I've ever owned in this price range. It's sturdily made in a color I love, deep red (the company that makes it offers a great selection of colors). The design itself is quite attractive, with a pleasant oval shape, large numbers which are easy to read, and a good grade of plastic. Best of all, the action of the function keys is very smooth. The keys on the last few stopwatches I owned had a rough action, and for the most recent one, that's what caused it to die. The left, top function key got stuck and couldn't be unjammed.

One downside--which seems to be consistent across all stopwatches I've owned--is that the instructions are hard to read. They are in small type, confusing and incomplete. However, my husband and I together were able to figure out something I never could with my last stopwatch, how to turn off the hourly chime. That drove me crazy with the other one because the clock on it ran fast so it never did chime on the hour. It was too much trouble to keep resetting the clock because I never used it since I wear a watch.

Tip for turning off the alarm which is not in the instructions: Follow the instructions to get to the alarm. Hold down the (R) right button and tap once on the (L) left button. You will see the alarm symbol go away. Tap it again to make it come back. If you set the alarm, frankly, I have no idea how to turn it off when it rings but this. If you tap on the (R) button once, it acts like a snooze alarm, and the alarm rings again in about sixty seconds.

I give this product high marks for the uses I mentioned.
text_fidelity_b: ACCUSPLIT Survivor II - S2XL Stopwatch, Clock

Twirling a hula hoop is one way to get the body moving and the heart rate climbing without the need for much space. If you want something like a hula hoop but with certain advantages compared to one, then you might like this Smart Hoola Fitness Hoop.

To use this hula hoop substitute, you put it on and attach the links. The weighted piece then twirls around while you move your hips. The hoop itself holds snugly to your body, so you don’t need to worry about trying to keep it up while you move your hips, like you do with a traditional hula hoop.

Putting this together is a little confusing at first, but once you get the hang of it, it’s not bad. The massage feature is nice and it’s something you certainly don’t get with a traditional hula hoop. The weight is just the right size. I was worried that it would be too hard on my back, but it wasn’t. I recommend starting with just 10 minutes then build up to the 30. If you can make a hula hoop work, then you can easily do this. If not, you can pick it up pretty fast.

I like all the new and improved variations on traditional means of fitness. This Smart Hoola Fitness Hoop is different, and in many ways, better than a traditional hula hoop and a great choice for those who want simple fitness and massage all in one.
text_fidelity_b: Weighted Hula-Hoops Smart Hoola Fitness Hoops with 24 Detachable Knots for Adults Weight Loss, 2 in 1 Abdomen Fitness Massage, Adjustable Hula Circles with Weighted Ball, Great for Women, Men

text_fidelity_a: Dsoon Trail Camera 4K 32MP Deer Cameras The first trail cam we ever purchased, while we were not trying to be cheap about it, because of our lack of experience at the time with trail cams, we also didn't want to spend a ton but the first one we had was around $129 and it was absolutely a joke.  The night vision on that cam couldn't have possibly been worse, unless it just didn't work at all, but it worked slightly, however definitely not good enough for $129.  The picture quality was that of a child's first camera, to say the least.  So we decided to give this Dsoon a try.  This impressive set, at the time of purchase also had a $10 coupon , making this trail cam $69 and I was willing to give this is a try after reading some reviews and considering it was half of what we spent on our first one.  Right out of the box, this trail cam is aesthetically cool and very sturdy, the camo makes it great for hiding on most of our trails.  Very impressed with the fact that it comes with the 32gb card and card reader.  I feel like what's most impressive about this trail cam is the quality video, not only is it extremely clear and detailed, but the sound and visual 4K is just beautiful.  The resolution is quite impressive, and definitely blows our first one out of the water on most aspects.  Motion detection is also extremely impressive.  Keep in mind, all of these features are subject to placement, so just know that you will need stable, line of sight.  In other words your quality of sound and video, along with performance is only going to be as good as your choice of placement.  I had a friend that wasn't particularly aware of height when placing their trail camera outside their back door and she didn't place it high enough and a racoon easily got it and destroyed it, so always be mindful of that.  You really can't go wrong with this little trail cam and again for the price, it's absolutely worth it.  This would make a great gift for any outdoors person as well.  I hope this review is helpful!

text_fidelity_a:
SPRI Stash It Belt One of the most frustrating things for me is if I want to go for a long walk in a rural area and I have to have a phone near by. I prefer to walk without a phone and such, but at times I can not escape the need to have a phone for an important phone call. I really don't like a fanny pack, as it is really big, but was looking for something handier.

WHAT IS THIS LIKE?
This stash belt is very thin. It is deceiving, however. The belt itself is a good quality stretchy elastic. It is heavy duty but not so heavy that it is bulky. There is a black clip in the back, and a slide to make the belt longer or shorter. The pack itself is 2 inches by 9 inches. However, it has a pleat in the top and bottom which make it bigger.

There is a water resistant lining in the pack, a front zipper, and a very thin reflective strip on the front. At full length, the belt measures 34 inches unstretched, and 41 inches stretched. The shortest is 24 inches stretching to about 32 inches.

HOW DOES THIS PERFORM?
When using this, I can put my smart phone into the pack, a set of keys and a few cards. I can also stick in a tissue or two folded small. A huge set of keys will make it a bit tight, but a reasonable ring of keys with several keys on it should be fine. The pack does stretch a little bit so that things will fit.

As far as use, I found that this is very handy. I have to stretch it a little tight so that it does not bobble around as I walk. That is okay though, because it holds it in place. Otherwise, the phone and things can make it sag a little bit. Finding the right tightness takes a bit of trial and error. I really appreciate having this as it makes it the closet to walking without anything that I have been able to get.

THE BOTTOM LINE
I really like this stash belt. It is handy, useful, and makes it so that I can go for long walks without bulky bags or packs. Safe and with decent capacity, I can carry what I want to have with me yet feel free and lightweight at the same time. With a range of sizes it will fit, many people would benefit from this, but if you are a big and tall man, it might be a bit tight.

RATING
Five stars for this. I really like it. It is handy and easy to use. I will update if I have anything else important to add in the future.
text_fidelity_b: SPRI Stash It Belt

text_fidelity_a:
KUGOO Electric Scooter, 800W Motor Off-Road Scooter, 10-INCH Pneumatic Tires Up to 25 MPH Motorized Adult Scooter, Electric Scooter for Adults, Pro Scooter, G2 PRO I have 7 scooters I've collected along the way to review and hands down this is the most fun one out there! If you're familiar with how an electric scooter works then this one is just like the others and will be easy to setup and get going. Took me about five minutes to unbox and get going! Even for newbies this scooter is plenty easy to setup!

One of the favorite things I love on this are the giant wheels- we ride on a concrete trail several miles across town and this absolutely grabs onto the concrete very well and is a better overall ride! My one complaint is the tires must be thin as on my fourth ride, one of them got a flat even though I didn't hit anything noticeable like glass or a screw. Nothing in the tire but it just started losing pressure on a ride and within a couple minutes the tire was completely flat and I was stuck pushing it home a mile. My suggestion is to get the tire size off the tire and immediately swap them out for solid tires! The air tires are a slightly smoother ride but you'll regret it when you're stuck pushing it home...
Edit: The air leaks out of the valve stem. I went to add some green slime and it did hold air but when I moved the valve stem, air comes out at the bottom of it... So the valve stem was faulty and the slime didn't help anything. I've been searching like crazy with no luck finding a solid tire to replace these with. Should have been on the scooter to begin with in my opinion.

Speed wise, I got this monster up to 29 mph and I'm a larger man (260 pounds) so that's a testament to this thing! It stands higher than your average scooter too which is weird at first but I fell in love with the added height nearly instantly!

It has a faster startup than other scooters that require more of a kick start. Which- be careful, that can be dangerous if you have the scooter on and are pushing it to park it before turning it off. I almost flipped mine backwards onto myself this way, it happens QUICK. So definitely turn the scooter (and any scooter) off before pushing around.

Battery life is fantastic- we ride several miles across town and back and I still have half a battery left after that!

Overall this is my favorite thing I've gotten on review and I've gotten big fancy electronics like big TVs, computers, etc... But this is my favorite toy I've grabbed, I HIGHLY recommend it! In the future I'll absolutely be buying another from this company!
text_fidelity_b: KUGOO Electric Scooter, 800W Motor Off-Road Scooter, 10-INCH Pneumatic Tires Up to 25 MPH Motorized Adult Scooter, Electric Scooter for Adults, Pro Scooter, G2 PRO

text_fidelity_a:
ZOOOBELIVES Ultralight Backpacking 32-50F Down Sleeping Bag - 27oz Ultra Compact 650 Fill Power Envelope Sleeping Bag for Hiking, Camping and Backcountry, Lightweight and Compressible – Alplive T400 I received this sleeping bag 5/26/2022. Upon unpackaging, this sleeping bag smelled absolutely horrible! It had a very, very overpowering smell of poultry. No way could I sleep in this bag on a backpacking trip with this smell.
This mission statement on their storefront "ZOOOBELIVES is the brand of ZOBON INC of its own kind, which prides itself in selling unique outdoor products of the highest quality.", does not hold true with this sleeping bag.
For $84 I would expect that the down used in this bag, would be clean and free of smells. Especially the smell of nasty feathers.
I washed this bag in the washing machine, and put it in the dryer on low heat. About 20 minutes into the dry cycle, the smell of this bag had our laundry room smelling like a farmyard!
So I pulled the bag out, and hand washed it. I had to drain the water and refill the wash tub twice, because the water was so dirty. And the smell. I cannot even begin to tell you just how bad it smelled. A mixture between a wet dog and a chicken farm. It was bad! So bad, that our washroom smelled bad enough that I had to Febreeze it!
I let the bag soak in the wash tub both times for 30 minutes.
After the 2nd soaking/wash, I rinsed the bag and the water was finally clean.
I then placed the bag back in the dryer and threw 3 bounty sheets in with it to make sure that the smell was indeed gone.
After about 2 hours in the dryer, the sleeping bag was completely dry. And the horrible stench was gone.
IF this company truly prides themselves on "Highest Quality" gear, then the QC for the down in these bags needs to be a lot better!!
I purchased a down bag from one of the major manufacturers of tents, and that sleeping bag had NO bad smells. And I have also purchased multiple of the packable down throws, and none of them have smelled this way!
In the pictures, you can see just how dirty the water was. The final picture of the bag in the wash tub, was after the 2nd wash and during the rinse. The water was clean. And the smell was gone as well.
So I spent 3 or 4 hours cleaning a "New" sleeping bag!
Now that it is clean, the loft is even better than it was before I washed it! I will update on the performance of this bag when I get it out in the woods.
It was purchased as a summer bag, so it should perform good as that. But, we will see.
text_fidelity_b: ZOOOBELIVES Ultralight Backpacking 32-50F Down Sleeping Bag - 27oz Ultra Compact 650 Fill Power Envelope Sleeping Bag for Hiking, Camping and Backcountry, Lightweight and Compressible – Alplive T400

It's been dropped a couple of times with no issues. I have only hand washed it, and so far no issues (only been a couple of weeks). It's cute, easy to carry, but when left in the car, it spits at me when I re-open it! A couple of other people have mentioned it on reviews as well. It's not worth me returning for that reason alone, but I would probably look elsewhere next time since there are so many other options.
Update - I've now had this a couple of months and traveled with it on an airplane. My old water bottles would occasionally "spit" from the pressure change on the plane, so I was fully ready (with my sleeve over the spout) to catch the water from this bottle. Oh, wow...it was like Niagara Falls! The funniest part was that the water ended up in my lap, so it looked like I just didn't make it to the rest room in time. The hook came in super handy when I wanted to clip it to the outside of my backpack.
The real reason I am updating my review is because it was hard to drink out of the straw due to the suction. As dumb as this sounds, I found myself drinking water less because of this issue. I went back and read some additional reviews and a couple people mentioned removing the little piece in the cap that effects the airflow. Eureka! It now works perfectly! I'll be using this bottle more often now.

The entire plastic ammocam smoked, then burned up -- battery, antenna, wiring and camera. Glorious billows of smoke that stunk to high heaven. Fried everything. Don't mess with burning lithium-ion batteries. And don't shoot them!

A perfect ending to a useless product.

I practice yoga regularly and am currently about midway through a yoga teacher training program. I own several mats, with the one I use the most often being [[ASIN:B009LHXD3O Manduka EKO Lite]]. This mat is on the thin side--which I generally like--and yet there are times when I find a bit of extra padding to be supportive.

The length of the SukhaMat worked so that it fit across my entire yoga mat. The width seemed a bit narrow, as I found myself adjusting the placement of the pad during use. As promised, the mat definitely did provide cushioning, yet I found the density of the mat to be a bit too much on the "squishy" side rather than providing firm support. And although the mat is supposedly made of foam, I found that it gave off a bit of an unpleasant, rubbery scent.

In the end, I didn't find this mat to be more convenient than standard yoga props such as blankets or blocks. Even rolling it up with my yoga mat for storage/transport was a problem--when I did this, it made my yoga mat too bulky, and it caused the SukhaMat to curl up on the edges rather than to lie flat. I can't say that this mat worked well for me, but it may be better for others who are in need of a more cushy product.
text_fidelity_b: SukhaMat Yoga Knee Pad Cushion – America's Best Exercise Knee Pad - Eliminate Pain During Yoga or Exercise - Extra Padding & Support for Knees, Wrists, Elbows - The Perfect Yoga Mat Accessory

Franklin Sports Badminton Net Set - Badminton Net Sets Up In Seconds - Includes 2 Rackets, 2 Birdies and Pre-Strung Net and Poles This is exactly what we were looking for. The kids love badminton and have been taking their rackets on camping trips, occasionally trying to play over a string or rope between two trees and making due with whatever kind of court that gave them (often with rocks, roots and bushes in and around the court) or they would play in the street without a net. This allows us to put the net wherever we want to without the pain of setting up poles and guy wires. It is fully self supporting, although a little tippy so we often weight the stand. It takes a little while to set up and has so far taken a little bit of parental help.

We had the net up within 15 minutes of it arriving at the house and played four hours. the poles have been run into and the net has been hacked on a bit and it has held up, and I expect that it will hold up pretty well. The rackets and shuttle cocks are not super super high quality, not as good quality as our older set, so we probably will not be playing with these. The big draw for this set is definitely the net.

If I had any constructive criticism, I would say, I wish it packed down a few inches shorter, perhaps four rather than three section to the net poles, and I wish there was a little more weight to the base or better way to secure it to the ground. There are spikes but they are small and depend on having permeable ground. These are minor, all in all it is a great set.
text_fidelity_b: Franklin Sports Badminton Net Set - Badminton Net Sets Up In Seconds - Includes 2 Rackets, 2 Birdies and Pre-Strung Net and Poles

My complaints are the same that everyone else has... The height of the bars is a bit high; you almost need a stool or chair to stand on to mount onto the bar. Same height complaint about row ups, but the chair fixes that problem too.

The bar itself is nice and strong and there is not twisting or torquing when using it. But by itself its a little on the wobbly side. The fact that the bottom rests on the door frame is what keeps it stable. If you're heavy enough the bars will flex a little on the ends but not much. I'm about 185 lbs and after the first few times you use it, its hardly noticeable.

The pads are soft and they seem pretty tough. They're not the grainy open cell sandable foam that a lot of pieces have. These are closed cell and just right.
